office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital, and transportation budgets, serving a two-year term.
race_blurb: An open seat between two Democrats: former Shoreline mayor Keith Scully and former FTC antitrust attorney Danica Noble, both dual-endorsed by the 32nd District Democrats and WEA-PAC.

candidates.summary: Shoreline councilmember and former mayor, attorney and former prosecutor, running on housing, climate, progressive tax reform paired with spending restraint, and limited AI regulation.
highlights: Calls the millionaires tax "the start, not the end" of tax reform and says Olympia needs to rein in spending [S3]
Would maintain the Climate Commitment Act and push toward 100% sustainable energy [S3]
Endorsed by the Seattle Times, The Stranger and Washington Conservation Action [S4]

taxes.basis: Supports the millionaires tax and progressive restructuring, but frames it as replacing regressive taxes rather than layering new ones and pairs it with spending restraint.

spending.basis: Says Olympia must rein in spending and earlier proposed a small across-the-board cut except education.

housing.basis: Mixes subsidies, tax credits and land trusts with streamlined permitting and support for state density mandates.

safety.basis: Cites bringing mental health professionals into the field in Shoreline; serves on the Regional Crisis Response Agency board.

climate.basis: Would maintain the Climate Commitment Act and push to 100% sustainable energy; former Futurewise legal director with conservation endorsements.

experience.basis: Ten years on the Shoreline council including as mayor, but no state legislative record.

immigration.basis: Supports banning masked law enforcement and defending state laws against federal overreach.

tech.basis: Favors limited, responsible AI regulation: disclosure, no AI in schools or with children, data centers only with clean energy.

candidates.summary: First-time candidate and former FTC antitrust attorney running on tech and AI guardrails, competition enforcement to lower prices, and school funding.
highlights: About 20 years at the FTC, including the antitrust case against Meta [S1][S4]
Would strengthen antitrust enforcement, ban surveillance pricing, and bar insurers from using AI to deny coverage [S3]
Endorsed by the Washington State Labor Council and Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates [S1][S6]

tech.basis: Campaign centers on guardrails for AI and tech targeting kids and workers, surveillance-pricing bans and limits on student data.

spending.basis: Calls for fully funding schools and investing in public hospitals while pledging to spend wisely with real accountability.

housing.basis: Pairs faster permitting and more supply at every income level with stronger renter protections.

experience.basis: First-time candidate offering federal enforcement expertise rather than an elected record.

healthcare.basis: Proposes stronger state insurance regulation and public-hospital investment within the existing system; no universal-coverage proposal.

immigration.basis: Opposes federal deportations of refugees and supports state help for refugees.

social.basis: Endorsed by Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates; no statement of her own on reproductive or LGBTQ+ policy.
